key_insight: LeVo 2 resolves the song-generation trade-off by using hierarchical token modeling for global planning plus track-specific refinement, then reconstructing audio with a diffusion-based codec.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical design for controllable full-length music generation systems that need both long-range coherence and high-fidelity vocal/accompaniment detail.
method: LeLM predicts mixed tokens first for semantic planning, then predicts vocal and accompaniment tokens in parallel for track-specific refinement.
A music codec diffusion model reconstructs full-length waveforms from the hierarchical representations.
Progressive post-training uses SFT, offline DPO, and semi-online DPO, with aesthetics-guided musicality conditions during pre-training.
evidence_signal: Expert listening tests and objective evaluations show improvements over open-source baselines across six subjective dimensions and competitiveness with leading commercial systems on several metrics.
watch_item: The multi-stage training pipeline is complex and may be sensitive to data quality, preference alignment noise, and optimization instability across stages.
paper_title: LeVo 2: Stable and Melodious Song Generation via Hierarchical Representation Modeling and Progressive Post-Training
